newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Oil slips as oversupply counters fund buying.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Oil slips as oversupply counters fund buying.

text.p: A tug of war on world oil markets saw bearish industry sellers outweighing bullish investment fund buyers on Friday, dragging crude prices lower.
London futures for bellwether Brent blend last traded at $20.00 a barrel, down 19 cents.
"I think the fundamentals are beginning to reassert themselves on the market both in Europe and the U.S.," said Nauman Barakat at brokers Prudential Bache in New York.
Traders said a lengthening queue of North Sea cargoes had deepened the gloom on the Atlantic Basin market.
But investment fund managers, taking leave of equity and bond markets, were again seen as net buyers of oil futures in New York.
"There's some evidence that the funds are taking on extra length," said an analyst in London.
"Some funds have switched from shorts (net sales) to longs (net purchases)," said Barakat.
News from Baghdad that Russia and Iraq had signed a $3.5 billion deal for Russian companies to develop the southern Iraqi Qurana oilfield also put pressure on prices.

Russian Oil Minister Pyotr Rodionov said the contract signed with Iraqi Oil Minister Amir Muhammed Rasheed would be implemented regardless of United Nations sanctions imposed on Iraq for its 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
The curbs place a blanket ban on investments in the country.
Dealers said the contract would not mean any extra oil on the market in the short term. But they said the possibility of Russia breaking ranks within the U.N. on sanctions had raised concerns.
Traders said the threat of a strike by workers at four Unocal Corp refineries helped underpin U.S. petroleum product markets.
Unocal employees in California issued a three-day strike warning, citing disagreement over a handover of ownership to new owner Tosco Corp.
Dealers looking to U.S. gasoline for fresh market impetus were disappointed.
Demand for gasoline will rise as spring approaches, but despite low U.S. inventories dealers have shown little interest so far in chasing prices higher.
"With gasoline unable to rally it's difficult for crude to stay at these levels," said a dealer.
